Let the vertices be  

\[
L_i=(i,0),\qquad U_i=(i,1)\qquad (i=0,1,\dots ,10)
\]

The bug starts at \(L_0\) and must finish at \(U_{10}\).
For each column \(i\) the only edges are  

* horizontal bottom: \(L_i\rightarrow L_{i+1}\)  
* horizontal top:    \(U_i\rightarrow U_{i+1}\)  
* diagonal:          \(L_i\rightarrow U_{i+1}\)  
* vertical:          \(L_i\leftrightarrow U_i\) (can be travelled either up or down, but only once)

Because the bug may never move leftward on a horizontal or diagonal segment, its \(x\)-coordinate never decreases.  
Thus after the bug leaves column \(i\) it can never return to it, so each vertical edge can be used at most once, **when the bug is first at that column**.

---

### Dynamic programming

Let  

* \(a_i\) = number of ways to arrive at the lower vertex \(L_i\) (before possibly using the vertical edge of column \(i\)),
* \(b_i\) = number of ways to arrive at the upper vertex \(U_i\).

Initially  

\[
a_0=1,\qquad b_0=0 .
\]

When the bug is at \(L_i\) there are three possible ways to proceed to column \(i+1\):

1. go right on the bottom horizontal edge (\(L_i\to L_{i+1}\));
2. go diagonally (\(L_i\to U_{i+1}\));
3. go up the vertical edge (\(L_i\to U_i\)) and then across the top horizontal edge (\(U_i\to U_{i+1}\)).

When the bug is at \(U_i\) there are also three possibilities:

1. go right on the top horizontal edge (\(U_i\to U_{i+1}\));
2. go down the vertical edge and then across the bottom horizontal edge (\(U_i\to L_i\to L_{i+1}\));
3. go down the vertical edge and then diagonally (\(U_i\to L_i\to U_{i+1}\)).

Hence

\[
\begin{aligned}
a_{i+1} &= a_i\;( \text{bottom}) + b_i\;(\text{down then bottom}) = a_i+b_i,\\
b_{i+1} &= a_i\;( \text{diag}) + a_i\;(\text{up then top}) + b_i\;(\text{top}) + b_i\;(\text{down then diag})
        = 2a_i+2b_i .
\end{aligned}
\]

Set \(s_i = a_i+b_i\) (total ways to reach column \(i\)). Then  

\[
a_{i+1}=s_i,\qquad b_{i+1}=2s_i,
\]
so  

\[
s_{i+1}=a_{i+1}+b_{i+1}=3s_i .
\]

With \(s_0 = 1\) we obtain  

\[
s_i = 3^{\,i}, \qquad a_i = s_{i-1}=3^{\,i-1}, \qquad b_i = 2s_{i-1}=2\cdot3^{\,i-1}\quad (i\ge 1).
\]

---

### Reaching the final vertex \(B\)

At column \(10\) we may end already at \(U_{10}\) (counted by \(b_{10}=2\cdot3^{9}\)), or we may arrive at \(L_{10}\) (counted by \(a_{10}=3^{9}\)) and then use the vertical edge of column 10 to go up to \(U_{10}\).  

Thus the total number of admissible paths is  

\[
N = b_{10}+a_{10}=2\cdot3^{9}+3^{9}=3\cdot3^{9}=3^{10}=59049 .
\]

Therefore  

\[
\sqrt{N}=3^{5}=243 .
\]
